title: Viewing Window That Reveals Both Turning Points of a Cubic
originalTopic: Viewing window design for polynomial extrema
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The default square window on many graphing tools clips the turning points of f(x) = x^3 - 12x. Locate the local maximum and local minimum of this cubic and use their coordinates to recommend a window [x_min, x_max] by [y_min, y_max] that displays every essential feature.

steps.title: Find the critical numbers
steps.explanation: Setting the derivative to zero gives x = -2 and x = 2, the only candidates for turning points of the cubic.
steps.why: A window cannot show the shape of a curve unless it contains the critical numbers where the tangent is horizontal.

steps.title: Evaluate the function at the critical numbers
steps.explanation: The point (-2, 16) is a local maximum and (2, -16) is a local minimum, so the interesting y-values span from -16 to 16.
steps.why: The extrema values fix the smallest vertical interval that must be visible.

steps.title: Add margins and state the window
steps.explanation: The x-span [-4, 4] places both critical numbers well inside the frame and shows the ends turning upward and downward; the y-span [-20, 20] clears the extreme values 16 and -16 with headroom.
steps.why: Margins of roughly 25 percent prevent the turning points from touching the frame edge, where they are easily mistaken for intercepts.
